title: Usage fingerprints and quota profiles — exploratory notes
body:
Purpose: quick exploratory writeup for a per-credential/per-route view that helps product, SREs, and devs understand not just "usage numbers" but usage behavior patterns (fingerprints) that should drive quota decisions and alerting. This is a working doc — sketch ideas + prioritized backlog items.

Context and problems we hear:
- Customers complain that per-key token counts are noisy and don’t communicate bursts vs steady traffic. Hard to tune rate limits without killing legitimate batched workloads.
- Support spends time triaging 'quota exceeded' tickets where usage is actually due to misconfigured retries or a runaway route.
- Product wants to offer smarter defaults for quota tiers but lacks signal about common fingerprint patterns across customers.

Primary user personas for this page:
- Platform engineer / SRE: needs to diagnose incidents quickly and see whether a key is abusive, buggy, or legitimately high-traffic.
- App developer: wants quick guidance on whether they should request quota increases and what to change in client behaviour (batching, caching).
- Product ops / CS: triage quota limit requests and tune default policies across customer cohorts.

High-level idea: "Usage Fingerprint Panel" (top) + "Quota Profile Timeline" (middle) + "Per-route Breakdown" (bottom). Interactions are filter-first: choose API key(s), timeframe, and then inspect fingerprint archetypes.

1) Usage Fingerprint Panel (single-row summary cards)
- Small cards for selected keys: name, tier, current quota cap, daily tokens, peak RPS, 95th percentile latency.
- One-line fingerprint summary: e.g., "burst-y: short spikes 10–30s; multiroute; high embed ratio" or "steady-batched: 99% calls single route /chat, consistent token-to-request ratio" (we show a short NLP-generated label + confidence score).
- Visual: mini-sparkline with shaded peak windows, plus a 1–7s microburst histogram under it to highlight microbursts that might trip token buckets.
- Reasoning: instant triage—SRE sees burst vs steady at glance.

2) Quota Profile Timeline (middle, main canvas)
- Timeline with stacked layers: provisioned quota, committed reserved capacity (if dedicated), tokens consumed, burst allowances used.
- Overlay-of-events: rate limit rejections, quota increases, customer support actions, canary rollouts. Hover reveals exact timestamps and ticket ids.
- Mode toggle: show normalized view (percent of quota) vs absolute tokens. Normalized is useful for comparing keys of different tiers.
- Actionable affordances: from any point in time, click to create a 'playback' — replay requests (anonymized) to reproduce spike locally in staging.

3) Per-route breakdown (bottom)
- Stacked area chart by route showing token share. Include tiny table to the right with per-route aggregates: avg tokens per request, median response size, error rate, retry rate.
- Quick filter to highlight routes that contribute > X% of tokens or routes with high retry ratios.
- Suggested next-step buttons: "Recommend route-level quota exception", "Flag for client fix (retries)". Buttons create tickets in internal queue with prefilled context.

4) Anomaly & Pattern Detection (side panel)
- Automated fingerprints we want to detect: microburst, steady drift, burst+decay (e.g., user churn), bot-like constant high-rate, multi-route scatter (indicates fanout).
- Each detected pattern has: severity (info/warn/critical), suggested remediation, example timeframe, representative requests (anonymized), and a one-click 'silence' or 'escalate' action.
- Important: detection thresholds are user-configurable per-customer and per-plan. Default presets per plan (dev/prod/enterprise).

Micro interactions and details:
- Hovering a sparkline shows both instantaneous RPS and token/s request for that timestamp.
- Drag-select on timeline to set a focused window and re-run fingerprint classification on that window only.
- Pin any expanded card to the top as a live watchlist (persisted per user).
- Export snapshot: CSV of route breakdown + small JSON containing anonymized sample request headers for replay.

Backlog groom (priority order):
1. Basic per-key cards + sparklines + normalized percent-of-quota toggle (MVP) — eng estimate: 3 wks (frontend + metrics query changes).
2. Per-route stacked area with quick filters and export (followup) — 2 wks.
3. Fingerprint classifier prototype (server side job that labels keys daily) — 3 wks (data infra + small model).
4. Timeline playback and ticket prefill integration — 2 wks.
5. Anomaly detection UI and config presets — 3–4 wks.

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- User can select up to 10 keys and see summary cards with normalized sparklines for last 24h and last 7d.
- Percent-of-quota toggle works and chart queries remain sub-2s for 24h window.
- Export CSV with per-route aggregates for selected keys.
- Playbook stub in product-ops for recommended default thresholds.

Open questions / decisions for product/engineering:
- Privacy & sampling: what is our policy for storing request samples used by playback? (need legal input).
- How to surface KMS/HSM customer requests where log storage is restricted? We should honor private customers by disabling sample export by default.
- Cost: classification jobs over all keys could be heavy. Possible approach: run classifier on top-N keys per tenant or run nightly with incremental windows.
- Should fingerprint labels be surfaced in API (so partners can programmatically act) or UI-only?

Edge cases and design constraints:
- Keys with very low volume: show a 'not enough data' state and avoid mislabeling.
- Multi-tenant dashboards: only show cross-key aggregation for keys within same org or with explicit shared view permission.
- Very large customers: consider precomputed rollups (minute-level) to keep the UI snappy.

Notes for design handoff (wireframe specifics):
- Card width: 280px, include three-line microcopy under fingerprint label (one sentence).
- Timeline: use 1px stacked area with 3-color palette for tokens/committed/burst. Provide high-contrast option for accessibility.
- Per-route table: sortable by tokens, errors, retries. Add small sparkline next to each route row to show recent shape.

Suggested follow-ups (who/when):
- Engineering (Arjun) to prototype queries and share cost estimate (due EOD next Wed).
- Design (Sofia) to produce 3 variations of the summary card by next design crit.
- CS (Ethan) to gather 5 recent support tickets where quota visibility would have helped; attach to ENG-1427.

Rough UX notes/fragments / brain dump:
- "Percent of quota" is way more meaningful to customers than raw tokens. Everyone asks, "how close am I to throttle?"
- Show TTL for quota reset prominently. People expect daily reset times vs rolling windows — make that explicit.
- Consider an "auto-suggest" that recommends changing burst window vs bucket size based on detected microbursts. Make it explainable.
- For multi-route fanout, show a mini graph of route fanout map (tiny node-link) that indicates how many downstream routes are being hit by a single client.

Appendix: links to related drive docs (for reviewer reference):
- quota-decomposition-journey-mapping-wip (see flow diagrams)
- token-usage-decomposition-brainstorm (good ideas on normalized UX)

Triage: drop high-level summary into CS weekly sync once initial prototype exists.

---
Last lines: this is intentionally light on exact copy; want design to iterate from these building blocks. Use this doc to seed a short design workshop (30–45 mins) with eng + CS next week.
